tldr: Three items land under the shared "autonomous driving" tag without forming one event. Two arXiv papers tackle unrelated problems (multi-agent common-sense reasoning for AV control, describing dataset differences in natural language), and Alibaba's Qwen team separately open-sourced a dedicated autonomous-driving model.
whats_new: Alibaba's Qwen team open-sourced a dedicated autonomous-driving model on September 7 — the only production release among the three unrelated items grouped here.
why_it_matters: For platform engineers the Qwen release is the one item worth a look as an open-weight domain model to benchmark against a perception/planning stack; the two papers stay in research territory for now.

beats.headline: arXiv paper proposes multi-agent orchestration for AV common-sense reasoning
beats.summary: Targets robust perception and decision-making in unseen driving scenarios.

beats.headline: Separate arXiv paper documents autonomous-driving dataset differences in natural language
beats.summary: Focuses on describing dataset composition, not vehicle control.

beats.headline: Alibaba's Qwen open-sources a dedicated autonomous-driving model

open_questions: Does Qwen's autonomous-driving model get evaluated or adopted by any AV stack outside China?
Do either of the two research papers see follow-on citations or production adoption?
take_for_builders: Building AV or robotics agents: benchmark Qwen's new open-weight autonomous-driving model against your current perception stack rather than expecting a broader agent-tooling angle from this group.
